findings.english_quote: The article and noun are feminine accusative plural, while θαυμασίους has the masculine accusative plural form under regular three-termination inflection. The intended sense remains clear, and the irregular agreement does not prevent a defensible translation.
findings.issue: The source note unnecessarily diagnoses irregular agreement. θαυμάσιος admits two-termination usage, in which θαυμασίους can be feminine accusative plural. The supplied article and noun support that ordinary morphological analysis; the printed form does not establish a source defect.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain τὰς θαυμασίους πράξεις. Remove the proposed correction τὰς θαυμασίας πράξεις and either omit the defect notice or replace it with a nonblocking morphological note explaining the common-gender form. No restoration or further print verification is required for this construction.

findings.english_quote: gave an account of the marvelous deeds
findings.issue: The narrative sense of ἱστορέω is defensible, but the note does not adequately explain its selection over the experiential sense of observing or becoming acquainted with the deeds. Although it lists “inquire into,” its appeal to the expressed object does not distinguish these readings: both can take the deeds as their object. The preceding companionship with the Lord makes experiential knowledge a material contextual alternative.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a note preserving “observed/witnessed the marvelous deeds” or “became acquainted with the marvelous deeds” as an experiential alternative, and explain why recounting them is selected in the main text. Alternatively, propose an experiential main rendering while preserving the narrative alternative and explaining the contextual choice. Any changed main rendering requires fresh review.
